name: Flamagra
editorial_article:
Flamagra, released in 2019 by Warp Records, represents the sixth studio album by the visionary American producer Flying Lotus (Steven Ellison). Following a five-year hiatus from his full-length solo discography after the critically acclaimed You're Dead!, this project emerges as an ambitious, expansive sonic narrative that synthesizes the artist’s disparate influences into a cohesive, fiery mythology. Ellison conceptualized the album around a central, metaphorical image: an "eternal flame sitting on a hill," an idea that became solidified after a chance encounter with the iconic director David Lynch, who lends his haunting, surrealist spoken-word performance to the album’s lead single, "Fire Is Coming."

Musically, Flamagra is a dense, high-fidelity exploration of jazz-funk, experimental hip-hop, and avant-garde electronic music. Across its 67-minute duration, Flying Lotus orchestrates a sprawling roster of collaborators, including Thundercat, Anderson .Paak, Little Dragon, Solange, George Clinton, and Denzel Curry, among many others. The collaborative nature of the album feels less like a series of guest spots and more like a carefully curated ecosystem of sounds. From the jittery, fusion-informed rhythms to the lush, atmospheric textures, the album balances chaotic, frenetic energy with moments of profound, meditative stillness. It is a defining work of the late-2010s experimental electronic landscape, solidifying Ellison's role as a vital nexus point between the worlds of jazz fusion and modern beat-making. By channeling years of disparate sketches and thematic musings into this singular, burning vision, Flamagra remains a hallmark project that captures the restless innovation of one of modern music's most unique producers. The album's structure—featuring 27 tracks—reflects a dense, almost overwhelming creative output that rewards multiple listens, shifting seamlessly between jazz improvisations, trap-inflected beats, and introspective ambient passages, all held together by Flying Lotus’s unmistakable production signature.
editorial_pitch: An expansive, psychedelic journey through the intersection of jazz-funk, experimental hip-hop, and electronica, Flamagra serves as a testament to Flying Lotus's mastery of collaborative world-building. Featuring an eclectic roster of guests, the album captures a central thematic tension—an "eternal flame on a hill"—that pulses through its sprawling, twenty-seven-track architecture.
